explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit that fires only in the original-input phase at steps 3-6 (mostly 3-4; never at t<=2, the delimiter, or the copy phase), almost always when the input is d (82% of mass) or s (17%), with a few on x. The bare condition (d/s input at t=3-5) covers 96% of mass but has 2% precision, so the unit also depends on the prefix. It is strongly enriched when the first token is z/b/k/l (z highest, about 9.6x lift), when the prefix has no digits, and when the previous token is d/u/i/r/t/s/x/j. The largest activations look like z z j u [d] and z l j s [d]. Adding these prefix conditions raises dev F1 only to about 0.41 (precision 0.34, mass recall 0.63). The remaining dependence looks like a distributed conjunction over the hidden state, not a clean token rule. I did not check what controls magnitude beyond the first token being z/b.
